categories.main_business_segments: WISCOM primarily operates in the manufacturing and processing of chemical synthetic resin materials and plastic products. Its main business includes producing PVC compounds and other high-performance resin compounds used in power cables, communication cables, automotive cables, interior materials, construction materials, hoses, and consumer goods. The company also engages in processing services, including compounding for major clients like LG Chem, and operates subsidiaries in China focusing on similar compound manufacturing.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes compounding technology that blends base resins such as PVC, PE, PP, PC, and ABS with various additives like plasticizers, stabilizers, and pigments to meet specific physical property requirements of customers. Production involves advanced compounding processes with specialized recipes (formulations) to produce high-value-added products including flame-retardant compounds, thermoplastic elastomers, and environmentally friendly compounds. WISCOM operates multiple specialized production plants and employs 3-shift operations to maximize capacity.
categories.primary_customers_markets: WISCOM serves key customers in the power cable, communication cable, automotive, shipbuilding, and general plastic product manufacturing industries. Major clients include leading cable manufacturers such as LS Cable & System, Seoul Cable, Doowon Cable, and LG Chem. The company’s products are used in diverse end markets including electrical wiring, automotive interiors, construction materials, and consumer goods. It also supplies processed compounds to LG Chem for ABS, EP, and PMMA products.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in South Korea with five production plants located in Gyeonggi-do and Jeollanam-do provinces. It also has two wholly owned subsidiaries in China (Wuxi and Jiangmen) that manufacture PVC and ABS compounds. WISCOM exports products to markets including Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Europe, and South America, with a focus on expanding overseas sales channels.
categories.supply_chain_position: WISCOM operates in the midstream segment of the plastics supply chain, specializing in compounding base resins into customized intermediate resin products. It supplies these compounds to downstream manufacturers of cables, automotive parts, and plastic goods. The company also provides toll processing services for major chemical producers like LG Chem, positioning itself as a key materials supplier within the value chain.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic R&D focus is on developing high value-added and functional compounds such as halogen-free flame retardant compounds, anti-tracking power line compounds, thermoplastic elastomers, and environmentally friendly products. WISCOM maintains a dedicated R&D team recognized as a corporate research institute, emphasizing import substitution of functional resins and responding to evolving customer needs. Continuous innovation targets new markets including UL-certified, automotive, power cable, and communication cable applications.
categories.revenue_model: WISCOM generates revenue primarily through the sale of compounded resin products and toll processing services. Sales are conducted mainly via direct orders and some through distributors, with payment typically in cash or promissory notes. The company’s revenue streams include domestic and export sales of PVC and other compound products, processing fees from LG Chem for ABS and other resins, and minor sales of related products like pigments.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: WISCOM is a leading player in the Korean PVC compounding industry, holding approximately 16% domestic market share. The market is fragmented with about 70 competitors, but WISCOM distinguishes itself through scale, advanced compounding technology, and strong partnerships with major chemical companies like LG Chem. The industry is oligopolized at the resin supplier level by LG Chem and Hanwha Solutions, with WISCOM positioned as a key downstream compounder and toll processor.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, WISCOM reported consolidated revenues of approximately KRW 112.3 billion, reflecting a 10.6% decline from the previous year. The company experienced an operating loss of KRW 2.85 billion and a net loss of KRW 476 million, marking a turnaround from prior profitability due to domestic demand weakness and intensified competition. Total assets stood at KRW 123 billion with equity of KRW 111 billion, and the company maintains a low debt ratio of 10.9%, indicating strong financial stability despite recent revenue contraction.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: WISCOM emphasizes its technological expertise in compounding to deliver customized resin products that meet stringent physical and safety requirements, such as flame retardancy and environmental friendliness. Its competitive advantages include proprietary formulation know-how, diversified product portfolio across multiple end-use industries, and strong R&D capabilities enabling import substitution and high-performance product development. The company’s scale, quality certifications (KS, UL, ISO9002, ISO14001), and strategic partnerships with major chemical producers further differentiate it in the market.
